prompt: You describe a lost item from photos so its owner can identify it. Write a clear description of the item.

candidates.hypothesis: Adding structured guidance to cover general, distinguishing, and personalizing details, while advising caution on uncertain claims, should increase captured tags and reduce wrong claims, raising net score.

Instructing the per-photo describer to report only clearly visible details without speculation, and having the merge model consolidate all unique observations, will increase coverage of distinguishable and personalizing tags while reducing wrong claims.

Instruct the describer to prioritize clearly visible distinguishing and personalizing marks while avoiding unverifiable guesses, and use a second pass to list owner-identifying marks, which should raise net score by increasing recall of unique details without adding wrong claims.

winner_cfg.prompt: You are describing a single photo of a lost item so its owner can identify it. Focus only on what is clearly visible in this photo. Include any text, numbers, logos, colors, patterns, materials, shape, wear, damage, or unique markings. Be specific: quote exact text, describe placement and size. Do not guess or infer details not visible. If something is ambiguous, say so. Avoid mentioning the brand or model unless it is clearly legible. Your goal is to capture details that distinguish this item from similar ones.
winner_cfg.aux: You are given several descriptions of the same lost item, each based on a different photo. Combine them into one complete description. Keep every unique detail from each photo, especially text, logos, colors, and distinctive features. Resolve any conflicts by favoring the most clearly visible evidence, and note if a detail is uncertain. Do not invent new information. The final description should be accurate, comprehensive, and help the owner recognize the item among similar ones.

candidates.hypothesis: Adding structured coverage of general, distinguishing, and personalizing visible details while requiring verbatim reporting only for clearly legible marks and flagging uncertainty should raise tag recall and reduce wrong claims, improving net score.

Adding structured guidance to the per-photo describer to focus on clearly visible distinguishing and personalizing details while avoiding speculation, and instructing the merge model to consolidate unique observations without adding unverified claims, will increase captured tags and reduce wrong claims, raising net score.

Adding a three-tier structure for general, distinguishing, and personalizing/condition details, with strict visible-only caveats plus a second marks pass that lists unique owner-identifying details, should raise recall of distinguishing and personalizing tags while reducing wrong claims.

winner_cfg.prompt:
You are describing a lost item from a single photo so its owner can identify it. Write a detailed, factual description based ONLY on what is clearly visible in this photo. Do not guess or infer.

Cover:
- General: type of object, color, material, shape, size, condition.
- Distinguishing: unique marks, logos, text (read exactly), patterns, wear, damage, attachments, accessories.
- Personalizing: anything possibly unique to the owner (initials, custom stickers, contents, specific wear patterns).

For each detail, state its location on the item. If text is visible, quote it exactly. If something is unclear or partially hidden, say so or omit it. Do not invent details. Be specific and precise.
winner_cfg.aux:
You combine per-photo descriptions of a lost item into one coherent description for its owner. Use ONLY the details provided in the per-photo notes. Do not add new information or infer.

Consolidate all unique observations, removing duplicates. Prioritize distinguishing and personalizing details that could help the owner recognize the item. Organize by feature (e.g., overall, markings, wear). If a detail appears in only one photo, include it. If notes conflict, note the uncertainty. Do not mention the photo number. Keep the description clear and factual.

candidates.hypothesis: Restructuring the single-call prompt to require compact coverage of every part's general attributes before listing distinguishing marks, while limiting verbatim quoting to short clearly legible strings and forbidding inference, should recover missed general and distinguishable tags and reduce wrong claims.

Adding a mandatory basic-attributes checklist and stricter rules for legible text and unidentifiable logos in the per-photo describer, plus instructing the merge model to include all unique general details first, will increase general tag recall and reduce wrong claims, raising net score.

Reworking the per-photo prompt into an exhaustive ordered checklist that forbids speculative identification, plus a compact second pass that only adds owner-identifying marks visible in the photos, should recover missed general, distinguishing and personalizing tags while holding wrong claims down, raising net score.

winner_cfg.prompt:
You are describing a lost item from a single photo. Write a factual description based ONLY on what is clearly visible. Do not guess or infer.

First, list these basic attributes in separate lines: type of object, primary color(s), material, shape, approximate size, condition.

Then add details in three sections:
- Distinguishing: unique marks, logos, text (read exactly), patterns, wear, damage, attachments.
- Personalizing: anything possibly unique to the owner (initials, custom stickers, contents, specific wear patterns).

For every detail, state its location on the item. If text is large, clear, and fully visible, quote it exactly. If any part is blurry, cut off, or partially hidden, describe its location and say it is illegible—do not guess. If a logo or symbol is not clearly identifiable, describe its shape and colors without naming it. Do not invent details. Be specific and precise.
winner_cfg.aux:
You combine per-photo descriptions of a lost item into one coherent description for its owner. Use ONLY the details provided in the per-photo notes. Do not add new information or infer.

Consolidate all unique observations, removing duplicates. First, state the item's general attributes: type, color(s), material, shape, size, condition. Then list distinguishing details (marks, logos, text, patterns, wear, damage, attachments), then personalizing details (initials, custom stickers, contents, specific wear patterns). Include every detail from any photo, even if it appears in only one view. If notes conflict, note the uncertainty. Do not mention photo numbers. Keep the description clear and factual.
